lens: Product systems and reliability — first encounter (simulated AI expertise/user lens)
reason: The public proposition and Precision Instrument hierarchy are clear. The reviewed student journey runs from published recruitment/preparation through application materials, explicit recovery choice and submission reconciliation. Original-resume disclosure accurately limits the privacy promise; pending case studies do not invent outcomes. The synthetic mobile close dialog makes irreversible consequences prominent and distinguishes submitted work from valid independent evidence. Local logs support substantial engineering checks, but these are not observed user success or hosted acceptance. Two acknowledgement gaps weaken the otherwise careful recovery model; address them before operational release. Broad world-class agreement remains unproven.

findings.evidence: submit() calls finishSubmission() for any response.ok without reading the success body. finishSubmission clears both browser recovery records and navigates with submitted=1. The actual API success contract is { applicationId } in src/app/api/apply/route.ts; unlike draft and release handling, this client path never validates that receipt. This is a source-demonstrated unchecked path, not an observed production failure.
findings.userImpact: An empty or malformed successful response discards the local recovery copy and advances as though submission were confirmed.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate the application receipt before clearing recovery; reconcile unknown or malformed success through the authenticated status endpoint. Add a focused malformed/empty 2xx submission case that verifies answers remain until confirmation.

findings.evidence: act() catches transport failures as only “Request failed” and returns false without refreshing status. RoundStatusControl.saveStatus at lines 60-66 consequently leaves the close dialog and its previously loaded coverage available after a lost acknowledgement. The database set_round_status commits an irreversible ACTIVE-to-FROZEN transition; a lost response cannot establish failure.
findings.userImpact: An operator can be told the request failed while grading actually closed, leaving a misleading recovery state at a consequential action. The supplied operator network-failure test covers the coverage GET, not a lost freeze POST response.
findings.suggestedFix: Give close-grading an explicit unknown-outcome state, fetch authoritative round status after transport failure, and require reconciliation before offering another confirmation. Test a committed freeze followed by a lost response.

notVerified: No staging, deployment, hosted Clerk/Supabase/RLS/storage/email integration or migration/application rollout was exercised. Log totals (673 Node, 709 SQL, 18 operator and 8 privacy browser checks) describe supplied separate local runs, not a new run by this seat.

No human task study, actual operator acceptance, live authenticated private-screen session, assistive-technology evaluation, physical-device or Safari/Firefox evidence. Captures reviewed include a synthetic operator modal.
Round coverage is explicitly advisory and can change before freeze; reviewed counts are not atomically bound to the closing write. Operator acceptance of that tradeoff remains unknown.

Client-approved outcome artifacts, Board resolution of resume-review policy and privacy retention decisions remain outstanding. No independent verification of organizational statistics or delivery guarantees was performed.
